The patient is a postoperative individual (3 days status post open cholecystectomy) presenting with acute systemic and respiratory symptoms: fever, chills, headache, pleuritic right-sided chest pain, and new productive cough. Imaging reveals right lower lobe infiltrates. Laboratory findings show leukocytosis without anemia or thrombocytopenia. No signs of surgical site infection or deep vein thrombosis (DVT) are reported. The clinical picture strongly suggests a pulmonary infectious process—most likely **postoperative pneumonia**, given the timing, symptoms (fever, productive cough, pleuritic pain), and radiographic consolidation. - **Key Diagnostic Findings:**

This summary reflects a focused, evidence-informed interpretation grounded exclusively in the provided dialogue and objective data.
